title: Four biomes, after the worldgen soil baseline
question: (1) Read as a climate gradient -- does wetland-to-rolling-to-canyon-to-arid look like four biomes, or like one biome with the plant count turned down? (2) Is arid dead in a way that reads as desert, or in a way that reads as broken? (3) Rolling shows individual trees where wetland reads as one continuous mass -- is wetland too dense, or is that what a wetland should look like?
context_md:
**What changed, and why you are seeing it.** The plant merge made water a real
second currency: a plant draws from soil `aux`, and that scales photosynthesis.
`origin/main` had no such draw at all. The consequence was the blocker this
branch opened with -- worldgen wetted soil only near water, so **six trees on
generated terrain grew zero leaves**. The fix was a climate baseline in the
worldgen moisture pass, derived from the per-column `aridity` that already
decides where trees get planted.

**These are the same four presets, same seed, same frame (10,800 -- a multiple
of the 3,600-frame day, so all four are at noon and none is mid-rain).** Nothing
here is hand-placed: every plant grew from the generator's own scattered seeds.

**Paired against a control run with the baseline switched off** (same build,
same seed, one line disabled), which is what the world did before:

| preset | living tissue, before -> after | decay events |
|---|---|---|
| wetland | 4,950 -> 24,160 | 113 -> 554 |
| rolling | **12 -> 14,166** | 0 -> 260 |
| canyon | **7 -> 6,064** | 0 -> 58 |
| arid | 0 -> 0 | 0 -> 0 |

The two small numbers are the finding. Rolling's control total of **12** living
cells is exactly its `life_scatter` count of 12, and canyon's **7** is exactly
its 7 -- meaning every seed the generator scattered was still sitting there as a
seed, ungerminated, for the whole run. Those biomes were not sparse before. They
were **inert**.

**What I got wrong on the way here, since it changes what you should look for.**
I predicted this would flood the whole map with "damp" readings and set moss and
decay running hot everywhere (moss spreads 175x faster on damp ground, decay
25x). Measured, that is not the story: only **2-7%** of standing litter sits
above the damp gate, because litter lies in the air block *above* the soil and
the field samples it there. Wetland was also already damp before the change --
the old pass seeded from the water table, not just from ponds. So the change is
much less about *dampness* than I claimed, and almost entirely about **plants
existing at all**.

**Arid is bare on purpose, but not for the reason I first said.** It is not that
its baseline falls under a threshold -- it is that any column drier than
`SAND_ARIDITY` carries sand rather than soil, and sand holds no water at all. So
arid grows nothing by construction, which is the desert-species gap you have
already logged rather than a tuning question.
